newsitem.title: SWEDEN: RESEARCH ALERT - SAS profits seen falling.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - SAS profits seen falling.

text.p: Danish commercial bank Den Danske Bank said higher fuel costs could knock 30 percent off Scandinavian Airlines System's (SAS') 9-month profits and downgraded the airline's shares and earnings estimates.
In a report dated November 1, the bank said the strengthening of the crown since last year and the sharp increase in jet fuel prices would hurt the carrier's earnings in the short term.
"As SAS discloses no information about its policy on hedging of fuel purchases, it is not possible to say when and how much SAS's result will be affected.

"Taken separately, more expensive jet fuel may reduce SAS's profit before asset sales by about 30 percent and we do not expect the airline companies will be able to pass on fully their higher costs by raising the prices", the report said.
SAS is three sevenths owned by SAS Sweden. SAS Denmark and SAS Norway own two-sevenths each. These holding companies are in turned half-owned by the respective governments and private investors.
The bank said it would downgrade the SAS Sweden and SAS Denmark shares to "underperform" from "match-", the SAS Norway share to "match-" from "outperform" for the coming 12 months.
"In our opinion, the SAS companies as a whole are priced too high, and the price trend since May has not yet shown signs of a changed relative pricing between the three stocks."
"Just as British Airways is trading at a premium to the sector as a whole, we believe that SAS ought to trade at a certain discount."
The company is due to publish its nine-month results on November 20.
